take_homes: Whatever I put in front of the model steers its answer. Vague input gives average output. A rules file the agent reads each session makes that repeatable.
The model grades its own work too kindly. Use a second reader with no context and check the claims myself.
Ask for a plan and approve it before the agent edits multiple files.

monday.move: Ask my controller to write a short rules file for month-end variance commentary and test it on last month's numbers, with a second reader checking the output.

monday.stop_condition: If it takes more than an hour, or the commentary needs more than light edits, I stop and report the cost.

misconception.why: It said the model stays the same and the user's context is what improves. That's a skill someone has to build, not a licence you buy. I still don't have a figure for what it costs or saves, so only shaken.

one_line: The context-and-rules-file part holds up. The personal website took most of the day and has nothing to do with my job, and I still can't tell the board what it costs or saves.
